review: Absolutely best poutine i've ever heard in my life and they definitely didn't hold out on portion sizes. I got the large poutine and they loaded it up to the brim, enough to eat for 2-3 meals myself. The gravy and cheese wasn't my favorite as they didn't have enough meat flavor in the gravy and the cheese wasn't melted but the chicken, fries, sausage was definitely the highlight to this poutine. The chicken was tender and juicy and was definitely different to all the poutines i've ever heard before. The staff tries their best to get through the line but it's worth the wait! I had to wait for 15 minutes in the afternoon but I left very satisfied with the food.

This was another poutine recommendation from Eater, and the tour guide from our food and walking tour corroborated that. When we showed up and saw the line around the corner, we figured that it must be good. We waited in line for about 30-40 minutes, but it was a nice evening. (I assume that waiting in that line in the dead of winter would not be fun.) You can order to takeaway, but they have seating indoors. We opted to eat there because poutine is better fresh. I read that the petit was still quite large, so we opted to split the petit. We both agreed that was a smart decision. The poutine was good, but the flavor of the cheese curds was muted by the shredded chicken and choriço. Their signature dish is their Portuguese chicken, and so I'm curious how that tastes when it's not covered in poutine gravy and cheese curds.

I'm a huge fan of Somebody Feed Phil, and after watching Phil's Montreal episode, I knew I had to make a stop at Ma Poule Mouillée. It ended up being one of the best meals of my trip. When I arrived, there was a short line, and as soon as I walked inside, the incredible aroma of rotisserie chicken filled the room. That's when I knew I was in for something special. I was told to order the wet hot chicken plate, so I did--and it absolutely did not disappoint. I also couldn't resist trying the famous chicken poutine. The flavors were bold, rich, and incredibly satisfying. The portions were enormous, too; there was easily enough food for several meals. Before leaving, I picked up a small homemade tres leches tart for dessert. It was the perfect ending to the meal. The cake was moist and delicious, and the caramelized burnt sugar on top added an amazing flavor and texture. I honestly wish Ma Poule Mouillée had a location in Detroit because this would become my monthly dinner spot without question. This place is the definition of "winner, winner, chicken dinner." If you're visiting Montreal, don't miss it--you'll leave full, happy, and already thinking about your next visit.

This has been a favorite Montreal spot of mine for over a decade. The last time I was in Montreal, these guys had fire and I was afraid they wouldn't reopen. I'm so glad they did and still just as good as always. We ordered the chicken legs, the poutine, and pastel de nata. The ordering can be a bit confusing as it's not clear what line is which. So the move is your line up and order by the cooks in front then move to the back to pay at the cashier. The portions are large and even the small poutine can feed a family. I lived the spicy chicken and pastel de nata. The poutine was good but didn't need the sausage. Overall very happy we revisited and that they're still amazing.

I could not decide what to eat for lunch on this rainy Sunday and I don't have any local currency. I'm on a credit only trip (just because I'm too lazy to deal with it) so that leaves Schwartz's out of the picture. I randomly came across this chicken palace and am so happy I did. If you enjoy rotisserie chicken, Portuguese chicken is your jam. This dude up front is a grilling machine and it's all charcoal. I got the half chicken with French fries and salad. It's a lot of food for under $12 US. I, of course, opted for spicy with extra hot sauce on the side. That stuff isn't very spicy but so very delicious. The chicken was moist and flavorful and the hot sauce was perfect with it. The heaping pile of fries was a bit overkill. There were a lot of Asians in there so you know it's a good deal. I'm Asian myself so I would know.

The chicken is tender, it's better with the spicy sauce. The portion is huge and you can definitely share with two people. It's very popular but I found the overall flavor is okay, not a complete wow. But the dessert was great!

We visited this place because we just had to try poutine and heard it was fabulous here. That is true, and you'll be sure after 1st bite.. Great fries, with chorizo + bits of chicken, good amount of cheese curds and finally smothered w/gravy. I thought the gravy might be an afterthought/not interesting- but no, it was delicious. You walk in the door and all you smell is chicken grilling+ chargrilled goodness. They offer a1/2chicken w/salad+ fries. Since we were ordering the poutine we didn't want those extra sides; we just ordered whole chicken. They'll ask, spicy or not? We got 'spicy' -basically the orange sauce in pics. It's not at all 'spicy hot' -but tastes garlicky, rich and delicious. Great choice. Chicken is Portuguese style; with a chargrilled taste, very juicy and well seasoned. Talked to several people who were near us eating about how great the food was, and found out that like us, several of them were out of towners who'd asked a local "where to eat" in town. Every single person was raving about how delicious it all was. This place is the Bomb! Absolutely a 'Do Not miss' in Montreal. The small poutine we ordered was huge! And the large sized poutine others bought was size of a ham on the large plate. Even with 2 hungry people and my Hubbie is a big dude, we brought almost 1/2 of our food home to finish the next day. Not bad for $34+ tax. PS One pic is from neighboring table's plate- the guy said "Please do take a picture. What a find! I can't believe this place".

A bounty of food comes with your half chicken and fries! The "golden row" of chicken twisting and turning while cooking definitely generates much anticipation.  I'll say half of the 1/2 chicken I ordered was definitely moist and tender, while the other side was a bit dried out.  The fat from the skin was nonexistent, so not much flavor other than the sauce that coated the exterior of the chicken.  While there was an abundance of fries, which covered every inch of the paper box, sadly they were neither crunchy nor crisp.  This was right after opening my box after I paid for my order. I also got the chicken sandwich which was juicer even if it was less majestic than the 1/2 chicken.  The flan dessert was somewhat forgettable, I left half of it behind. There was a line up to order but it moved well.  There is seating inside however the tables and chairs were in need of a good wipe down.

The BEST POUTINE & BBQ chicken i ever had! It was the best food we had from Montreal. I've been to La Banquise for poutine multiple times and LB's good but this chicken and chorizo poutine is superior! Perfect potato fries, bbq chicken, cheese curds and gravy! Dont forget to ask for their spicy sauce on top! (Not spicy at all, just gives extra umami!) This place also gets long queue but much less than LB and it moves pretty fast! Their service is fast and efficient. While u are waiting, u can see how they cook their chicken on the Portuguese grill. I want to try bbq chicken with their hot sauce next time when I visit Mtl again. PS. Get large!! And pastel de nata is just ordinary.

They have a tiny dining room. Their reputation brings many people coming. Locals and tourists line up around the block. Their chicken is delicious. Their poutine is huge. We ordered it loaded but I would order it without the chorizo. It's a little much.

I found myself at Ma Poule Mouillée as part of a food tour I was on. We were not told in advance which places we were visiting, so it was a pleasant surprise to find out that this was on the route. While I didn't know too much about this spot, I was aware of its popularity and that they served good poutine; needless to say, I was looking forward to checking it out. Ma Poule Mouillée is a Portuguese restatuant that specializes in chicken and poutine. We were there late morning so it was not crowded, though I was told it's normal for a line for form around the block during peak times. Our tour guide also mentioned that this place, along with La Banquise which sits catty corner, are two of the most popular places for poutine in the city. We were here for poutine - specifically, we got the variety topped with chorizo and roasted chicken. It was delicious - the fries were crispy, and the combo for the chorizo and chicken with the gravy and cheese curds really made for an elevated poutine. We didn't have time for anything else, but what we had was enough to make an impression. Overall, Ma Poule Mouillée was a total yes - this was one of the best poutines I've had in a while and I would definitely return the next time I'm in Montreal.

Want a Thanksgiving feast? I would say order the number 8. We had Portuguese meat, rotisserie chicken all in gravy on top of fries. I would say it reminded me of a heavy Thanksgiving meal. It was good. Don't get me wrong. The line was a bit long outside but once you get in, you order, wait for you food, pay, and then find a table to eat. It's small inside but you can grab a seat if you're patient. They also have a spicy sauce you can add to your meal that was pretty good. It's definitely worth a try but I think there are so many different poutine places I would try around Montreal.

Their gravy is delicious. Chicken is falling off the bone, it's cooked so well.  The portions are huge - my wife couldn't finish her "small" poutine, and I couldn't finish my portion of chicken legs with salad and fries. There is limited seating and no one seats you, so you have to watch for tables to free up and grab one while being in line for the food so having company helps!

I had so many recommendations to try this poutine in Montreal and it did not disappoint. The location is actually a Portuguese chicken restaurant but they do a poutine that has 2 full legs of chicken and sausage on top of your usual squeaky cheese curds, crispy fries and piping hot gravy. The portion was massive. We ordered the large poutine and it only cost $19.00. I think what makes this dish is the chicken, which is cooked to perfection with crispiest skin. The service was quick and you could see the chicken being roasted on the spits. The restaurant itself is set up as take out. You order and then find a spot to sit. Pretty spacious and lots of seating available. We went on a Monday morning (10am) during the winter so there was no line up. But I have heard that it can get very busy. We also got the eggs tarts which were delicious. Great recommendation.

This place was super busy and had a line but did move quickly. It was super packed when we went and therefore had to take our food to go and eat at our hotel. The place is definitely smaller inside but nice, clean, cozy and friendly staff. The food was amazing!!! We probably could have ordered a small poutine since we also had fries with the half chicken but no regrets! Best poutine we had for sure during our trip. Highly recommend!
Some of the best roasted chicken I have ever had. I would come just for the chicken, no poutine needed.

The line was put the door for good reason.  I ordered the chicken sandwich and they pulled it right off the grill and put it on amazing Portuguese bread.  Get the food to go and have the best Portuguese chicken and/or poutine in Montreal. Everyone was friendly and the whole place smells delicious!

Their grilled calamari and Portuguese chicken were AMAZING! The chicken still tasted delicious even when it was cold. They truly worked some magic with their sauce. I didn't try their famous poutine, and now I really regret it. I'll definitely be coming back when I get the chance!

Hands down the best poutine fusion in Montreal. The Portugese chicken compliments the poutine very well and definitely a dark horse in Montreal. They don't seem to get as much attention as some other poutine places, but don't sleep on this experience. For their price, it is a lot of food, one large serving of their 19$ grilled chicken with sausage and poutine is a great meal that will last you the entire day, it was more than enough for two. They debone two legs of chicken on top of the poutine that they pulled fresh off their grill! Service was fast, there is plenty of room to eat at the restaurant and they have a separate counter for the pastries. We had to get some of their Portuguese tarts (10$ for 6) and they were also amazing. Creamy, custardy, perfectly baked. It reheated well in the air fryer when we brought some back as souvenirs to enjoy. This is a place worth stopping by in Montreal, poutine in one hand and a batch of tarts for dessert on the other.

A Portuguese restaurant that is serving up the best poutine I've ever had. It is piled HIGH with chorizo, chicken, gravy and curd. The flavors are so warm, it is the perfect thing for a chilly day. This poutine could easily serve 3 people so keep that in mind when ordering it. Try your best to save room for dessert so you can try their pastel de nata

I was probably the most excited to try this place during my trip, and it really didn't disappoint! We came on a Friday around lunch, and I was happy to see that there was no line. It's pretty small inside with only a handful of tables and high chairs. We got the small poutine to share, and man, this bowl was hefty! It was a perfect amount of food for two people. The chicken was so moist and flavorful. They definitely don't skimp on the gravy - every inch is drenched. The chorizo wasn't quite what I was expecting. It wasn't my favorite, but everything comes together so well that I didn't mind. I wish I had room to try the pasteis de nata, but I guess I'll just have to come back. This is such a unique take on poutine! It's a must-try for anyone visiting Montreal.

The Portuguese chicken poutine here is literally top tier. The mix of the chicken, chorizo, and sauce is elite, and the portions are huge. Honestly, the only reason it's not a 5-star is because the line is always insane and it gets super crowded inside, but the food low-key makes up for it. Def a must-try in Montreal!

I was very surprised by this one. It is better than the guy across the street!   The gravy has a more deep flavor and the service (petite) is enough for two people that aren't extremely hungry Yum!  This is the place in Montreal for poutine

Holy s&$t this was amazing poutine! Worth the hype and worth the wait. Line seemed long but didn't take too long. It smelled so grilled and delicious in there. This was also recommend by a few locals to try as well so I would highly suggest eating here when you're in Montreal!

The Portuguese chicken was the one thing my partner absolutely wanted to try while we were in Montreal, so we ended up waiting for them to open while sitting on a bench on a cold March morning. They noticed us peeking in and invited us to come in early which was so kind of them! We got the first chicken of the morning and booked it to the train station to enjoy it, and it did not disappoint. Incredibly flavorful and moist. Next time we're in Montreal we will definitely be stopping by again to try some more of the menu!
Great chicken--so soft and moist. Gravy for the poutine was a little too sweet for my liking. I would love to eat more of that chicken tho

Don't let the lines deter you!  We arrived a little after noon on a Friday and made it to the front of the line within 20-25 minutes. We were handsomely rewarded with the most tender, juicy, flavorful chicken paired with crispy, house-made french fries and a salad (for health).  Seating was a bit of an issue, but I would've gladly eaten this meal on the curb.  It was THAT good!
This place is so tasty! Service was streamlined and fast. So much food for the price. The spicy chicken wasn't too spicy but overall very juicy chicken. They know what they are doing!

It's all about the chicken nothing else. I had the #11 salade florea a huge salad topped with plentiful and borderline obscene amounts of chorizo and chicken.  The chicken was so juicy, tender and unbelievably flavorful that it outshined everything else. We also got a petite (trying to be healthy here) #8 poutine with chicken and chorizo and the #12 combo veronique with chicken, chorizo, fries, and salad.
The line was down the street when we arrived, but don't be discouraged! It moves quickly. The poutine is wonderful and such large portions! We split one and still couldn't finish it!

To avoid long lines, I got here at 10am.  Also, make sure you push the door to enter, don't be like me and pull  :)  I knew what I wanted, so I got #8, small with couple drinks, egg tart and blonde donut thing. The poutine was decent.  I liked the chicken, it was moist, seasoned well and I would been perfectly fine just ordering the chicken by itself.  The whole plate as a whole, few things they could done better. I wish they added more gravy... if they layered it, it would have helped.  After the fries, add the gravy, then the cheese, chicken and sausage and another layer of the gravy.  After you eat the top, once you get to the rest of the fries, there's no gravy leftover unfortunately.  I don't know if you can ask for additional gravy on the side or if you need to pay for additional, but it would have helped to have more gravy. The interior was small, but plenty of seating to enjoy your food.  Egg tart was decent, but it would been a lot better if served warm.

Ma Poule Mouillee is a place where dreams come true. After reading Maria's review back in 2020, I knew I had to visit this spot if I ever found myself in Montreal. Well, I am so glad I did! We visited for lunch and there was a line around the block. Now with a ton of amazing spots in Montreal, you may be thinking is it worth waiting in line? Yes, yes it most certainly is. Once you make your way inside they have a great assembly line going. You order, then make your way down to the register. By the time you make it to the register, your order is waiting for you. Here is the time to grab extra sauce, we did not and I was regretful. The Portuguese chicken was moist and delicious, their sauce is just so freaking good. We also ordered the petit poutine, and let me tell you nothing was petite about that thing. My friend and I could barely make a dent in it. But it was also so flavorful and delicious. We rounded things out with some orange Sumol (the best flavor) and a pastel de nata. They have a variety of bar seating/tables around the restaurant. Even with the long line we were able to find seats to eat without an issue. If I'm ever back in Montreal, I will never not go here. The best!

Wow! A line that goes out the door and locals and tourists enjoy the food. Huge portions. Who knew rotisserie chicken could be so flavorful? I had the chicken and chorizo poutine, and wow, I could not finish my small portion. The gravy was delicious with bits and pieces of chicken and chorizo over crispy fries I love this place!

Absolutely one of the best Portuguese chicken places in the plateau borough. The chicken is super tender and juicy, and the piri piri sauce has to be some of the best I had. Very nice kick of heat with amazing flavors from the various spices. This place gets packed up very quickly if you are planing on eating inside the restaurant. However, parc La Fontaine is across the street, which offers lot of picnic table to sit down at. 10/10.

The best rotisserie chicken ever! Wow. This place gets super busy (rightfully so) and usually the line is out the door. Very minimal seating so plan accordingly. The Portuguese chicken here is mouthwatering. So flavorful, so fresh and very reasonably priced. Absolutely love this place.

Wow! This place was popular! I was visiting Montreal for the weekend and the first thing we did was go to Ma Poule Mouillée for some poutine! We ordered the small poutine with chicken and chorizo. I also ordered a half chicken platter and asked for rice instead of fries. For the drink, I saw that they had some Portuguese sodas! I got a passion fruit soda, it was good! We hovered around waiting for somewhere to sit. The poutine was delicious! It was a hearty meal.

I had to try their poutine as it was highly rated from poutines lovers. They are just across the street from La banquise and near LaFontaine parc, so be aware there's always a line to enter, but ut worth it to have their good food.. Their chicken poutine is excellent and on my top5 poutine in Montréal. Service is quick and efficient and once you're in you don't wait long. Il fallait que j'essaie leur poutine car elle est très bien notée. Ils sont placés juste en face de la banquise et près du parc LaFontaine donc préparé vous à attendre un peu car il y a toujours une ligne. Mais l'attente en vaux la peine car leur poutine est excellente, en fait c'est dans mon top5 des poutine à Montréal. Le service est rapide et dès que vous êtes entré vous n'attendez pas longtemps.

I first heard about this place on "Somebody Feed Phil" on Netflix. On my train ride up other passengers were discussing it. Except for the line wrapped around the corner, this place lived up to the hype! I had the Louis Cyr (1/2 chicken, fries and salad) and it was soooo good. The poutine looked great but for a number of reasons, it didn't fit into my needs. But everyone who ordered it was more than satisfied! The service is like a cafeteria line and I don't speak French but the staff is dedicated to working it out. The restaurant is kind of small but I had mine to go, so I didn't have to contend with finding a seat. I definitely recommend that it gets added to your list of places to eat in Montreal.

Had to come and try the chicken poutine! Overall: 4/5 Food: Chicken poutine 4/5 - I thought it was pretty goods; I'm not a huge poutine person, but was recommended it from someone in Toronto. I wouldn't necessarily tell someone to go out of their way to try this, but it was good! Mind you, I would have probably loved a chicken sandwich more, but tried this instead. Ambiance: 2/5 - it was so busy for takeout and the tables are in the same area, so wasn't the most comfortable seating arrangement. Service: 5/5 - they're very efficient, fast, and friendly. Had a great system going on!

That is the beauty of travel, you come up with something that you will always remember. This is not super fancy, or fine dining, in fact, this is your daily around-the-corner restaurant, but trust me, this is the best rotisserie chicken with potatoes I ever had. and I mean it. Especially Potatoes - what is this? super soft, not dry, juicy - how do they cook it?  I know a thing or two about cooking and I know my boiled potatoes can never be this soft. and though this is super popular across social media, - it deserves all those hypes. Luckily, I reached by 12 so I did not have to be in the 40 mins, 1 hr long line. I did not try their poutine (to be honest- I did not like the idea of it) I ordered-     1/2 Chicken served with fries & Salad. and being how greedy I am with food; I was about to order 2nd item - but as usual "an unknown hero (aka my wife)" came to save me and said- "let's finish this first then we will order again". and glad, she saved me because that one order- we both were not able to finish that- it was too much for us. not sure half chicken is how many pieces, but it was like 2 legs, and one breast with wings - with like 10-15 pieces of "amazing soft juicy [and I know I never going to have them in the future, no matter what unless I visit Portugal or visit Montreal again] potatoes", with salad at the side. man, if I visit Montreal again, trust me I will visit for this only. Quantity: too much, one item can be enough for 2 people unless you are Dwayne Johnson Ambience: In two words, very cool. I like how the establishment has managed to have a decent amount of seating while keeping the disturbance of the line flow to a minimum... first you order at the entrance and then you pay. There are a couple of two 6-seater tables and 6 long stools facing roads. that it Price: it was our cheapest and best meal of the Montreal trip- that says enough about this. Ma Poule Mouillée is a counter service restaurant - great food for a reasonable price.  The place is popular, drawing a varied clientele.

Everyone on the internet says this is the best place for poutine. We ordered a half chicken, which was way too much for two people, in our opinion. We are usually big eaters, but with the poutine, you can probably do a smaller chicken. We also did the poutine, with all the fixings, as recommended. The poutine is great on its own! It's so big, you'll definitely feel stuffed after eating some of this and some of the chicken. The chicken was like most roasted chicken places, it was good but nothing out of this world. You come for the poutine. The place gets crowded so beware of that. Staff wasn't the nicest, but it's expected from places that are so crowded that are often frequented by tourists. In my opinion, skip the chicken, focus on the poutine. You won't be disappointed.

I was never overly interested in poutine (sorry, I can hear the gasps! lol), but when in Canada, right? OMG- their chicken & poutine was top notch. There was a small line around 8:00pm on a weekday, but nothing that was bad. The chicken was absolutely, hands down, AMAZING. The pastel de nata was the best follow up dessert. I'm not going to lie, I also ate the leftovers for breakfast, too :) Seating is not really great for young kids (mostly high tops with just a few tables), but we just ran it back to our hotel! Would highly recommend!

Nice neighborhood gem! This place was recommended by a friend and it did not disappoint. Definitely a local spot because I wasn't sure what to order and the staff expected that I should. They were extremely helpful though. I ordered the spicy chicken poutine. It was served hot! It was delicious but way too much food for me to finish in one sitting. If you're in the area, do yourself a favor and check this spot out!

reviewer: Mr F G And Mrs M S.
review: We both love poutine. We decided to give this place a try. The poutine here were the best non classic poutine we've ever had. If you love poutine, this place is a must try. It's amazing! Generous portion! The line can be quire long but it moves pretty quickly. Highly recommended. We'll definitely go back!

I'll give a low rating because of the experience. Super busy with a line out the door and hectic inside.  I don't understand the menu so I talk with the person taking orders (not the cashier) and ask for the most popular item or what she recommends.  We go over options and I'm choosing something with options large and spicy. Almost certain a to-go person took my order but the cashiers have no idea and just gave it away.  Time passes and everyone behind me is getting their food so I ask if I need to order again.  A cashier talks to the woman I put my order with and tells me they're making it now. An order pops up that no one claims, so I ask is that mine -- and I guess it is.  If someone in the back ordered the same thing and took it, I'd still be in line. Food-wise, I'd give it a 2-3 star.  Very bland and not spicy.  Would stay away from #8 and not get large
Great poutine, can be easily shared between 2-3 people with ease. Do not expect to get any seating here, as it is busy and the line never stops -- takeout is recommended

By far THE BEST poutine I've ever had. Everything was delish! I got the poutine with the chicken and chouriço and my sons got a half chicken and the other poutine with just chouriço. Amazing!!  A must try. The line goes quick and the staff is friendly. The place is small so it's a little crowded so probably best if you take it home to eat unless u get lucky and find a table. Can't wait to come back

We got the half chicken to go and we were able to replace the fries with only salad. Service was friendly and fast.  Orders were placed at the front and then picked up and paid for at the back. Back at our hotel, we dug into our meal and the chicken was very moist and well seasoned.  We got the spicy sauce but it wasn't uniformly applied on our chicken so there would be bursts of heat in some mouthfuls but not others.  It was possible that the spicy sauce was reduced by the salad dressing.  However that did not distract from our enjoyment of this chicken.  It was one of the best we've eaten in a long time. Overall a definite repeat should we come back to Montreal.
Ordered the Floreana Salad and didn't love it because the chicken was too fatty... the chorizo was good and the portion was huge though. Also loved the sauce. But I prefer shish taouk type chicken.

Chicken was amazing. Seasoned beautifully and the charcoal flavor is wonderful. We arrived around 7:45pm on a Sunday evening and waited about 30 min. The ordering/paying/pickup process is pretty hectic once you get inside. They fill orders from the line as the food is ready so you're not always called up numerically by the number they give you when you place your order. I'd seen on prior reviews that they had rice instead of fries, but that was not the case (only fries listed on the menu and I asked about rice - not available). We also asked for the spicy sauce but they forgot to include so I was disappointed to not have a chance to try it. We ate in the store but the checkout line was so hectic I didn't feel Iike trying to go back to ask for sauce (and have them attempt to charge me again). I made only a small dent in the gigantic box of fries that came with my chicken. The person in front of me bought 10 pastel de nata and sold out the shop so I was also disappointed to not have a chance to try. I got the half chicken with fries and salad and my husband got the chicken on dinner salad (pretty large). Both are fairly large portions for the price. The crusty dinner rolls ($1) are also tasty! I'd probably go back - but would try to go earlier in the day.

This place is great. The poutine with chicken and sausage seems to be the most popular dish and it's solid, but the chicken is great on it's own or in a sandwich. The fries are very good on their own as well. There is usually a line outside the door but it does move quickly. Plenty of seating inside but it's self seating so you will just need to see what is open. Baked goods like the pasteis de nata and other things are really good so don't miss out on those. Great place to visit if you are in Montreal.
Great place!! Very tasty food! Good prices. Bad part, it is always crowded. Go early or you will find 45 minutes of waiting.

On the quest to find the best poutine in Montréal, we had to visit the highly recommended Ma Poule Mouillée. They specialize in Peruvian rotisserie chicken, and the platters themselves look amazing. But, the poutine was out of this world and such a run take on the Canadian classic dish. The chicken was perfectly succulent and crispy, and we loved the tangy hot sauce that topped it all. It's more of a takeout place, and was pretty crowded. But, if you wait about 5 mins a table should open up.

Also can't leave Montreal without trying poutine! Heard this place is better than La Banquise so stopped by for lunch. When you enter, you first place your order with one of the servers. Then you make your way to the cashier area and pay when your order is ready. There are several tables but this place is popular so plan for takeout if you come during the lunch rush. The menu is entirely in French but if you're here for the poutine, which most people are, it's #8 on the menu and you have the option of ordering either the small or large size. Unless you come with a party of more than 5, would recommend getting the small because even that is a huge portion. We did see a group of teenagers order a small each, which had us worried because it's basically a heart attack on a plate. Very heavy, greasy, and salty. Something I would try once but probably not have again in the near future. Sort of like the case with Chicago deep dish pizza haha. I did enjoy the rotisserie chicken and cheese on top of the fries though but was not a fan of the chorizo because it was too hard and salty.

We love Portuguese chicken and we're excited to find one in Montreal. It's cooked the classic way over fire and rotated. We ordered a whole chicken what I thought was supposed to be small fries and a small salad but they were huge The chicken was tender. And actually fed the two of us for a couple of days. There was a huge line around the corner, but someone suggested we call in the order and it was ready in 15 minutes so we didn't have to wait in line. Highly recommend.

Now I see why this place was recommended by everyone online of where to eat poutine in Montreal. I got the small #8 ($14). It was an enormous portion for a small and the container had to weigh more than 2 pounds. The chicken had a pleasant grill taste to it in the cards along with the chorizo made for a perfect meal. The rich gravy was amazing and the french fries held up to it and all the toppings.

Phenomenal chicken...likely the best I ever had.  It was perfectly roasted and seasoned.  Words cant really describe it.  I ordered the #2 spicy, which is a half chicken with fries and salad.  It was a lot of food, but overall its a great value. They also have a ton of French and portugese pastries. In terms of service, if the line is long it will take a little time (estimate 5-10 mins) before you get to the order window, which makes the service seems slow but rest assured these guys are working their butt off.  Once you order, the food is prepared quickly. There is indoor seating, but if the weather is nice get it to go (take away) and sit out on a bench or at the park. This is hands down a must try when in Montreal!

So many places online said this was the best poutine in Montreal, and it didn't disappoint!! I'm not the biggest poutine fan, but this was delicious. It's like gravy and cheesy goodness with super tender chicken. There's also sausage on it for meat lovers. Portion was huge for a petit size and it lasted me two meals. Service is rather fast. You order in this line at the counter and can watch them make it. It is hard to find seating inside, but you can get your order to go or sit in.

The yummiest Portuguese grilled chicken in Montreal came with a load of fries and a fresh salad, especially the sauce. oh, Chorizo Sausage is so good too.  got the #8 The place is small and very noisy, but they have some tables for dining in. You need to wait in line for at least 20 minutes or more but Worth the wait. Food: 5/5    Service: 4/5  Atmosphere: 4/5

Located in the Plateau Mont-Royal neighborhood of town, MA Poulle Mouillée is a very popular, no-frills spot that's as famous for it's insanely long lines and wait times as it is for their succulent Portuguese style chicken. And while trying to get that aforementioned chicken can easily require standing in a line anywhere from 45 minutes to 90 minutes, most loyalists would say that it's absolutely worth the trouble and I would agree. Jean-Jacques Rousseau once said "Patience is bitter, but its fruit is sweet" and boy was he right. The chicken coming out of this place is absolutely insane. It's full of flavor, it's moist and it is one of the bites of food I've had in a very long time. Depending on what you order, the contents of your box might change a bit but I recommend you get the "Le Tremblay" option for $16CAD which features some chicken breast, a ton of fries and a side salad of greens with shaved carrots in a delicious vinaigrette. Don't share, just chow down in shame. It's greasy, it's tasty and full of flavor. If you're super hungry (you must be American - hi!) you can get other, larger options: ones with chorizo or even befana and while the first is scrumptious, the befana was nothing to write home about and ordering it isn't something I'd do again. Honestly the Tremblay is plenty of food. Service wasn't particularly friendly or fast - but man, it just doesn't matter. Just get in line and you'll be rewarded with a Portuguese feast which shines some spotlight on a cultural piece of Montreal that few other places can showcase as well. A+

A must go-to spot whenever I'm visiting Montreal. This small no-frills dining joint specializes in fresh and tasty roasted Portuguese chicken, and it is always done excellently. The portions are always huge for the price (one is enough for two meals honestly), and the chicken is super moist, juicy, and tender. Their poutine is also amazing, one of my favourites in Montreal. Service is curt, but you're here for the food and it comes out fast. There's limited tables/seating available on the inside and sometimes a line to get in during the busier season. Definitely recommend adding this spot to your Montreal foodie itinerary.
What a wonderful surprise, my wife I just walked in without knowing anything about this restaurant and enjoyed a wonderful meal....my grandson would love it here.

Oh my goodness! Go here, order everything and enjoy life!!!! We tried almost everything and it was all so good. Even the dressing on the salad was amazing. Parking can be a bit difficult to find, but I promise it was well worth circling several times until we found a spot. Portions are large, so I do recommend getting smalls and sharing. Next time I would definitely ask for extra salad dressing on the side to dip things in. Don't forget to try dessert too! The nata was the perfect amount of sweet and and soft but firm custard.

Exceeded my expectations! We were visiting from California and don't speak French (google translate is very helpful for the menu!). The woman helping us was very kind and helpful with any questions I had. We ordered the half chicken with fries and salad and everything was so delicious!!! The chicken was so good and tender. I'm still thinking about this meal! I have a sensitive stomach (mainly sensitive to dairy) and I did end up with a slight stomach ache afterward so I'm thinking there may be some sort of dairy in the sauce or something, but honestly worth it! Definitely a MUST TRY

Large portions. I was expecting more flavor in the chicken. Spicy was not spicy, mild at best. Good to be a potato farmer in Canada. The side of fries was nauseating. Some parts of the chicken were chewy from being dried out. Order at counter. Quick service. Definitely had a fast food vibe in terms of ambience. I won't be craving this anytime soon.

Why is is so hard to order??? As an American trying to get some poutine here it was so difficult. Their menu didn't even look like there was poutine on it so we didn't know how to order and when we asked they were so stuck up so we ended up not even getting the poutine and just chicken and fries. But even so the portion was more like fries with a side of chicken. They are absolutely not friendly to Americans at all because they were already giving us snarky looks when we were literally just trying our best to figure out how to order. I understand that we may come off as "annoying" but like help us out here. Overall the food we got was OKAY. Nothing special whatsoever. Felt like regular chicken and fries to me.

Insanely delicious! Some of the best food I had in Montreal. Don't be deterred by the line -- it moves fast. They give you a TON of food: we made the mistake of ordering a large poutine in addition to our meals but a small would have been so much more than enough. The chicken is tender and so flavorful. The poutine is really special; covered with Portuguese chicken, chorizo, and gravy. And the chicken sandwich was also delicious. Come here if you're in Montreal! Just order less food then you think

Yummy dishes. I have been here 3 times and ordered different things. Each hit the spot and was satisfying. Thanks to the chef for doing a good job. The staff took my special instructions and it showed in the result.

This Portuguese chicken is amazing. It's a must try if Montreal. The line can be very long and seating inside is limited. Worth the wait though as the chicken is very flavorful. You can see them making it fresh as you step up to order. Half chicken comes with fries and salad. Good portion size

My friend and I were stuck in Montreal and were recommended by a Canadian friend to go try some "well-known" poutine. I've never been a fan of poutine in the States, but fully acknowledge I've probably never had high-quality poutine. We read the reviews for this shop and fully expected the long wait. Service was fast and NOT rude (we read many reviews saying they were rude), and we made sure to grab some egg tarts on the way out the door. We ordered the #8 poutine half size and did not regret it. Overall, the poutine was incredibly savory - would highly recommend getting a salad or soda to cut the salt. Each item in the poutine was quality! Fries were crisp (not soggy under the gravy), gravy had a nice flavor, chicken was moist and the skin was a nice touch, and cheese curds were tasty with a nice chew and flavor. Very busy inside on a Sunday afternoon, most folks order and grab takeout. Lots of families too. Friend's Review: "The chicken was the best thing. Just go and get the chicken."

The line is long but it moves fast! I had to let a couple people pass me because I was still taking in the menu and the ordering system. You basically get in line and order while youre moving along, then pay once you reach the register. I got a small #8 (came with cheese, chorizo and the portuguese chicken) as well as one portguese tart. The tart was cold but divine flaky goodness. The poutine, while a small size, is probably enough for 2-3 people to split. My favorite part was the crispiness and the flavorful chicken. There are a couple of tables in the area across the street, as well as a park you can take your poutine to eat in if you dont opt to dine inside.

With all the rave, I was really excited to try this for one of my dinner meals. We went at 8pm and yes, there is a long line around the corner.  And yes, it did moved fast. We waited 30 mins. The order system is very chaotic.   First a lady approached you and you tell them your order,  then a second lady comes to you while the line moves towards the register, you tell her your order again shouting on top of your lungs through this opening on the glass.  She packs your order, put it on top of a tray, and then to the register to pay. But by that time, you really lost track, which is your order, and you have to repeat your order over again. It got really confusing, the yelling, the language barrier at least for a first timer. The food, chicken was only ok.  It's not as moist as expected. Actually, dry.  The rave about poutine was too salty and overwhelming.   $3.50 for the Salad was a  fancy little salad. It's got the nice vingarette dressing.  I loved my salad. Came the desert.  The Portuguese egg tart was not what excepted. The filling is not a cream but a custard cake like texture.  Nevertheless, it's not that sweet and love the texture of the crust. Lastly, I also got a flan.  It was overly sweet, and the texture is not consistently smooth. I am glad I waited to try what the rave is about. Otherwise, I wouldn't get to write this review.  For the food and service was OK.  Probably won't go back for the second time.

There's  lots of hype on social media posted about Ma Poule Mouillee and I was excited to try it. I was a bit skeptical if it would actually live up to its name. Goodness I was pleasantly surprised to find that this was indeed a very moist fire roasted Portuguese chicken. I am always reluctant to order chicken in an establishment as it's oftentimes dry and overcooked. In my opinion condiments and sauces should enhance what you are eating, not be a necessary addition to revive your dish. If you arrive during peak dining hours, be prepared to wait on a line that extends outside of the eatery. It does go quick though cause  the staff behind the counters are efficient like well oiled machinery. I ordered a half chicken with fries and salad, two orders of a chicken quarter which also came with the same sides as well as a large poutine with chicken, chorizo, cheese curds and gravy. You are also asked if you'd like a mild or spicy sauce which they top onto your chicken. For my after dinner goodie, I got traditional flan, coconut flan as well as a cream cannoli for good measure. They had a nice selection of Portuguese desserts and breads. Additionally I saw two types of flan, and Portuguese egg tarts as well as typical French goodies yum! Entrees are packed in to go boxes as well as your side salads. That is a bonus as I do not like my cold mixed salad greens in vinaigrette touching my hot food. The portions here are generous and you more than likely will take your leftovers to go. There is decent indoor seating for this cozy establishment. Although every seat was taken, by the time I placed my order I was able to secure a table. Be aware that if you are a serious condiment lover, such as myself they do not give you more than one or two tiny cups per entree. When I asked for another small portion of their house made sauce the lady at the counter charged me a dollar. Not sure that is the case for everyone though cause there were plenty others asking for extra. I am guessing it depends on who is at the checkout counter? All in all it was a nice experience and the chicken was very memorable especially the chicken chorizo poutine which they are known for. I would eat there again for sure.

BEST POUTINE IN MONTREAL. Hands down this was bomb and there is a reason why there is such a long lineup that goes around the restaurant. #8 Bon les portugals font de la poutine ($18) ~ SOOO GOOOD the chorizo was so flavourful and delicious with their roast chicken. The cheese was perfectly melted and the gravy was so flavorful with the crispy fries. The cheese pull was insane and sooo good. Probably the best poutine ive ever had and 10/10 would come back just for this. It was good and delicious. Perfect for sharing as well. They roast the chicken fresh and daily and it makes the poutine 10x better. Overall a place I highly recommend because of how good it is.

I always visit here whenever I'm in Montreal! Love their portugese chicken and their portugese tart! Got their #8. Bon, Les Portugais Font De La Poutine (Poutine with Chicken and Chorizo) and their #1 Le Tony Alves (whole chicken) Portions were massive, and their chicken is seriously top notch! Love how well the flavours work with the poutine. Definitely recommend getting a drink to go with your meal since it can get a little salty near the end. But superb chicken!

A warm and filling meal for the soul. No frills order and grab your food at the counter spot, expect a line around the corner. It'll be about a 20-30min wait. Their poutine is topped with cheese curds chicken and chorizo - a large is more than enough for 3-4 people to share, it's filling and heavy. The whole chicken is a bit salty and so are the fries/ chicken chorizo combo. Nice to try once while you're in the area! Their egg tarts are yummy but are served cold, they taste much better warmed up in the oven - they're sold for $2 a piece or $10 for 6

Huge portions, did not expect the large to be that big. Grabbed the poutine and their egg tart to try. The poutine was really good, maybe the best one I've had so far but it did get a bit tiring towards the end. I find that the sauce was a bit too much. I liked the chicken, it was juicy and had lots of flavour but the gravy overpowered it. I enjoyed the egg tart, it was nice and creamy.

I came to Montreal during restaurant week and out of all of the delicious meals I had during my stay, this one stood out above the rest. I had seen a picture online of the fish that I wanted, a #8, which is a rotisserie chicken and chorizo poutine, I opted for "hot" (more piquant) sauce as well.  I opted for the small size as I wanted to eat a lot more that day and I'm honestly glad I did.  I can eat a lot of food but the amount that they packed into that small, aluminum container nearly had me bursting at the gills; cheese curds are no joke! This was one of those meals where you take a bite and are immediately in another world, where nothing else matters, and all you want to do is keep eating.  At first, I was devouring my meal but as it quickly started to disappear, I knew I had to savour it and make this moment last as long as I could. The inside, though small, had comfortable seating, with plenty of views of the surrounding neighborhood.  Though I thought this place would be touristy, I was eating with locals and construction workers.  Sitting there eating, I felt like I knew a secret that other travelers did not. For dessert, I got two pasteis de natas to really still down that Portuguese flavor. Do yourself a favor and come here.  I am honestly kicking myself that I didn't make it here twice during my four day stay.

Wow, first time trying poutine and I'm glad I came here to try it. Everything was in french but I managed to order poutine with everything on it. It was a delicious surprise and it surpassed many disco fries I've had in the US. The place is small and busy but the line moves quickly. There is not alot of seating so maybe ask for it to go if you don't find any.

Not too much seating in this restaurant but the food is absolutely amazing! I wished we had another day to go back and get more chicken! We stopped here because of the somebody feed Phil episode and true to what was said in the episode, the chicken is so juicy and flavorful, it's delicious. We were able to order in English and the lady behind the counter gave us suggestions on what to get. Nothing was disappointing. The Portuguese tarts were all very delicious as well. Salads were fresh. This does seem to be more of either a take out or eat quickly then leave, not necessarily a nice sit down dinner place. Definitely in the list to come back here when I visit.

Best chicken ever!!! OMG The French fries!!! Were awesome! The service is Great! The ambiance excellent! A lot of people but the guys inside the kitchen work very hard and fast   So everyone gets their favorites and enjoy!

I always recommend Ma Poule for their poutine! Their poutine is loaded and there's a hefty amount of protein from the grilled chicken and chorizo. Their portions are huge, so a small could fill you up, but a large makes it easily shareable. Their Portuguese roast chicken is also very worth trying! You can opt for a whole or half chicken. The serving sizes here are pretty big. Most of it comes with a side of fries and salad, but you can also just opt for the chicken alone. It's super tender and juicy! A very good post workout meal There might be a long line sometimes, but it moves rather quickly and the staffs working their hardest. There's ample indoor seating. You won't be allocated any seating. It's more of a cafeteria styled establishment, but I notice a lot of people eating outside as well.

If you're looking for a delicious poutine to have and share with multiple friends, look no further. We shared the petite poutine size between two people. If we were hungry and wanting that as a meal, it would still be very filling. The fries remained crisp and were clearly freshly fried. The gravy and cheese curds hit the spot. They also have many other great options with their freshly cooked chicken and a small bakery. The service was quick and the tables in the corner allow for quick seating to enjoy your meal and watch the park scenery outdoors. A great place to stop by for anyone who enjoys poutine.

Always stop into Ma Poule Mouillée to get my Portugeuse chicken fix in. We dropped in on a busy Wednesday afternoon (around 1:30pm). Not much has changed other than a small increase in prices. Prices include all taxes. - Combo Veronique (#12) ($15.00) - still a massive portion of fries. Chicken was tender and juicy. Chorizo had a nice kick. Good flavours. Salad is nice to offset the heavy carbs but it's always overdressed. - Nata ($2.00) - light, creamy and flaky. Always a filling, satisfying meal at MPM. Now if only they would offer their poutine in half sized portions.

Been to MPM a few more times since my original review so I decided an update was in order. It's a great spot to grab food and head over to Parc Lafontaine. We dropped in on a Sunday afternoon (around 2:00pm) and it was busy. We lucked out and snagged two tables at their patio outside. The menu is up on the walls; the menu du jour is a nice change up. They had three options (calamari, mixed combo, beef brochette and salmon). Trip #1 - Combo mixte ($14.00) - such a good deal. You get a salad, fries and meat; chicken (two thighs and a drumstick), pork chops and sausage. I have no idea how you can finish this alone but it's perfect for sharing. Pork chops were incredibly tender, sausage had a nice bit of heat and the chicken was moist. Get it piquant (spicy!). - 4x Natas ($1.50) - still as good and creamy as last time. Totally hit the spot. Trip #2 - Tony alves (#1) ($15.00) - whole chicken. We got it spicy. A little greasy but overall, pretty good. - Grilled calamari ($15.00) - this took forever to come out and it was a really small portion. Quite oily but not bad. Probably not worth the price point. Stick with the chicken. - A salada matilde (#10) ($9.00 large) - we got a large salad without the chicken. The best part was the homemade honey Dijon salad. - Bon, les Portugais font de la poutine ($14.00 large) - poutine with São Jorge cheese, chicken and grilled sausage. This was the best out of three poutines we ate (the other two were from La Banquise). Good fries, good cheese and tender meats. A small ($9.00) is more than enough. - 2x Le p'tit talbot (#5) ($6.00) - chicken sandwich for my cousin's road trip home. - J'adore mon choriço (#7) ($12.00) - an entire grilled sausage. They put spicy sauce on this as well. Good flavour and well spiced. - Pain grand-mère ($4.00 for 12) - my aunt bought a dozen Portuguese buns for home. - Natas ($1.50), coconut tart ($1.50), peach tart ($2.30) and almond tart ($2.30) - had to get my nata fix in! Still so good and creamy. Other tarts hit the spot. Always come back to MPM to satisfy my Portuguese cravings.

I had a difficult time figuring out which Portuguese place to hit up with my limited time in Montreal. Should I go to good 'ol reliable, favourite Romados or try one of the new players in town? After much debate, I decided to check out Ma Pouille Mouillée as I kept on reading so many great things about them. Located across the street from La Banquise, the inside is actually quite spacious. Several tables to sit at but be like everyone else and take it to Parc Lafontaine for an impromptu picnic. Hours are bomb. Everyday open early and late till 10:00pm! The menu is up on the wall and prices already includes all the taxes! Stand in line and order. It's like an assembly line. As you make your way down, the till is at the end where you can grab drinks and desserts. - Le Louis Cyr (#2) ($11.00) - half a chicken with fries and salad. Portion size is huge! A mountainous amount of fries and chicken. I should mention that I attempted to eat all this by myself - don't try this at home folks. Slather on the spicy sauce. Chicken was flavourful, tender and moist for the most part. Couple pieces of white meat that were too dry. The salad was great and the vinaigrette was addictively delicious - Natas ($1.50) - natas are in the back near the counter so don't forget to order one. Man, I miss good natas. This one was superb. Perfect amount of sweetness, flaky and slightly torched. Make sure you go to at least one of the many, many Portuguese places while you're in town.

Glad we "chickened out" and tried Ma Poule Mouillée. With a fun shop name, this is now among the most popular Portuguese chicken rotisseries in Montréal. Despite no lineup in the mid-afternoon, it was still quite packed with happy diners & folks ordering takeout. A whiff of aroma came from the rotisserie as it turned open whole chickens in unison. Staff at the counter happily processed food orders. For takeout, I had their famous poutine with Sãn Jorge cheese, chorizo & grilled chicken. At the pastry display, I couldn't help but try their Portuguese egg tarts (natas). A collective assembly of the shop's best offerings! Egg tarts were loaded with sweet doughy custard and a crackly crust composed of flaky layers. The packed poutine was oozing from the container with toppings. Its pulled chicken was moist with seasoned slow-cooked grill flavour, which was more noticeable than the chorizo slices. It blended well in melted cheeses, gravy & spicy sauce over the fries. I noticed the saltiness of Quebec food along with its bold flavours. For $12, it's amazing that the "small" poutine was enough for two meals. Bravo to the owner Tony for turning his passion for Portuguese chicken into one of the most popular cheap eat-outs in town.

Ma Poule Mouillée, can you expand to the US? We need restaurants like this. We ordered poutine and it was one of the best poutines I ever had. The chicken was moist, the cheese curds were plenty, and the gravy soaked in the fries was so delicious. Everything just works for this dish perfectly.

I came to Ma Poule Mouillée for dinner a while ago and got Number 8: Bon, Les Portugais Font De La Poutine, Petit. The rotisserie chicken in the poutine was excellent. It had nice flavour, quality bits and pieces of chicken, good fries, gravy, and cheese, and everything was good together. It was also an extremely high value meal and the food is enough for two people. This is a must try stop in Montreal and I'd give it 9.3/10

I came here for dinner recently and got Number 8: Bon, Les Portugais Font De La Poutine, Petit. The rotisserie chicken in the poutine was excellent. It had nice flavour, quality bits and pieces of chicken, good fries, gravy, and cheese, and everything was good together. It was also an extremely high value meal as it only cost $11 and I only finished ~half in one meal.
Took forever but was soooo good definitely recommend the poutine and the bakery section, cappuccino was so yummy

No parking and there is a line up great food - worth the 45 minute drive . The staff is really friendly . The place is small and priced reasonably. The chicken is amazing. This one of the best places in Montreal for Portuguese chicken . They have amazing fries. There Peri peri sauce is to die for They only thing is it hard to get a table so prepared for take out. This is a real winner

We were told about this place for great Portuguese chicken in the east end of Montreal. Ma Poulet Mouillee on a Saturday at 7 pm the line is crazy long . It was sure worth the 1 hr drive . The staff is friendly and helpful. We scored  a table and they have Biodegradable Cutlery . We were 2 and decided to order a whole chicken, medium salad  and small fries. The fries are amazing double fried and crispy. The chicken was tender and juicy and seasoned nicely. The Pri Pri sauce was not to spicy and it was great. The portions are large and there was even left overs. This is a sure winner and we will be back. This is where the locals eat

I ordered the poutine and the chicken with fries. The poutine was well seasoned, lots of gravy and was a good price for the portion. But the other meal -- it was dry and lacked flavour. I ended up going back to the restaurant to ask for some extra gravy and hot sauce, which made it better but it was more of a Poule Sechée than Poule Mouillée. Overall, I probably won't come back because I've had better but it's definitely not a bad spot, just not for me.

When I am in Montreal, I eat...and eat...and eat....I try as many restaurants as I can, sometimes, just a small sample of each...just so I can savor the particular flavors.... I had heard about this chicken place and I needed to try it.  It's a casual place with a funky menu, so you can pick a meal by the "name". Opened to the public since July 29, 2013, Ma Poule Mouillée is a great casual restaurant on Le Plateau Mont-Royal. The history goes like this.....from a young age, Chief Tony Alves was working with his uncle who had a restaurant. From that moment he permeated every movement his uncle baker made and learned every he could. With a dream and a clear idea in mind, Tony Alves did not hesitate a second to open his own restaurant. From then on, chef Alves learned to conceive a very special spicy sauce. For, as the chef says, it is the sauce that makes the difference, because everyone is able to grill a chicken. I really enjoyed this delicious Portuguese chicken roasted on charcoal.

Portuguese chicken should be on everyone's itinerary to try. We hit up Ma Poule Mouillée for a late lunch. It was packed on a Wednesday afternoon with the line backed up to the entrance. Wish they offered a half portion for their poutine. - Combo Véronique ($15.00) - grilled chicken, chorizo, fries and salad. This is more than enough for two people. A massive amount of fries. Chicken was flavourful, tender and juicy. Chorizo had a nice kick. Salad is overdressed. - Nata ($2.00) - creamy goodness. Make sure you get a Portuguese egg tart to try. Come hungry to MPM.

Super duper long lines at both lunch and dinner, try to get there early! Line moves fairly quickly, it's just a bummer to wait in the heat or rain, bring a bottle of water or umbrella Very simple and casual interior. One large table to seat 6 and the rest are bar seating around the perimeter. Try to decide on your meal while in line, the staff taking your order don't speak much English so you'll need to give them a number. You can customize your order with a bunch of sides. I highly recommend the potatoes over the fries. They are LEGIT. The roast chicken was solid, like a fancy pollo loco. The hot sauce is a $1 but is worth it for that extra kick. It's not very hot, just adds some nice flavor.
Honestly the best poutine i had in Montreal. Chicken js so flavorful and the addition of portuguese sauce is on point. Natas were great too. I miss this already. Must visit in montreal
Best chicken salad I ever had! The chicken is excellent. Our tour guide recommended it. Great choice!

Absolutely fantastic. I had the half chicken with rice and potatoes, and the flavours were just amazing. The chicken came off the bone so nicely, and the rice and potatoes were extremely delicious. The place itself is nice on the inside too, and the server was quite helpful in explaining their most popular dishes. It was awesome seeing the chicken being made as well right as you walk in. Highly recommend!

We walked by this place on our way to the park and saw a line outside, so naturally I looked it up to find out it was a Portuguese roast chicken place. I've never had it before and decided to give their takeout a try when we got the chance. My friend and I came by to pick up some dinner on Saturday around 7:30, and it wasn't too crowded. They have some tables for seating, but it's nothing fancy as this is a fast casual type of place. Looking around, I noticed that all food, whether it's dine-in or to go, is served in takeout containers. They serve their chicken in a variety of ways - by itself, with side of fries and salad, in poutine, etc. We ordered half a chicken ($8.27) as well as a small poutine ($9.57). Typically their poutine uses both chicken and chorizo, but we asked for chicken only to accommodate my friend's diet. I definitely liked the roast chicken more than the poutine. The skin was very flavorful, just not as crispy as I like since the chicken was served with some juice in the container. I was also expecting a more fragrant roasted flavor. The poutine was just okay... keep in mind, though, that I am not a poutine kinda person, and we didn't eat it until maybe 30 minutes after getting it, so the fries were a bit soggy by the time we ate. My favorite part of this dish was the gravy. I enjoyed the chicken and am glad we tried it, but it wasn't different enough from other roast chicken for me to come back.
We ordered the poutine, chorizo and rotisserie chickens and they are so good and serving sizes are generous too! The chicken was moist and crispy!
Such amazing poutine with chicken and chorizo.  Chicken is a must!  Two large poutines is enough for 6 people as whole dinner. Get it to go, sit at park and chow down.  Nata is great as well.

I learned about this restaurant from a show on Netflix and I walked 3 miles to get here from my hotel. This place was my first experience with poutine, and unfortunately I don't think that any other place will be able to live up to the taste of Ma Poule Mouillée. I got the large number 8 spicy, the chicken and the sausage were amazing. Be prepared to wait as the line was around the corner, the service was quick but the space inside is limited. All worth the wait.

Came here for dinner after a road trip from Toronto. There was a huge line out the door, even as there was freezing rain and 20°F weather. I already wrote this spot down when I researched places to eat in Montréal, although a convenience store owner nearby also named this shop as a recommendation. We waited around 20 minutes in line. Inside was packed, probably due to the weather, but also it just seems like a really popular spot to eat chicken. I noticed a lot of people were eating family style. We ordered at the counter and picked up our food as we paid by the cashier. We got a half chicken, a couple of salads, and a poutine. We got the egg tarts for dessert. Everything came out quickly. The bag and containers itself was quite oily. The chicken and poutine were incredibly salty. It was distracting from the actual flavor of the food. It's a good thing that we ordered those side salads because I don't think I would've gotten through the meal without it. The portion was also more than enough for our small family to share. I wish the meat was juicier as well. The best thing we got was the egg tarts. I don't know if it was bad luck, but I would not go here again based on this experience alone. I hope it was bad luck. It was not worth waiting in the freezing rain for.

It's always funny to experience what Montrealers think of as spicy. Either they forgot I wanted my sandwich to be spicy or, true to form, it was just very wimpy err subtle. I mean subtle. The chicken here is good. 15 minutes in line good? Sure. 30+? Nope. But the reason to come is actually the pastel de nata, which as good as what you can get in Portugal. I'd come back here in a heartbeat for one of those.

Delicious food. Incredibly busy, but I would honestly drive back from Connecticut USA just solely to eat here. My husband's family is from Portugal and they gave it all thumbs up as well. I will be dreaming of this food for years!

Got the whole chicken #1, poutine #8, strawberry tart. Chicken is juicy, not dry, but no smoky flavor. Poutine & tart are both good. Cramped restaurant, 1 bathroom, English menu is towards middle, small, taped to plexiglass.

We're from Las Vegas and despite many trips to Canada, we've never tried poutine. This restaurant was featured in Netflix' "Somebody Feed Phil" and looked like the place to start. We got poutine, salad and whole chicken to go. The service was quick. The prices were reasonable and the portions are huge. The salad is basic   The chicken was moist and delicious. The poutine was MUCH better than I expected. I will have to do two hours at the gym to atone.

Chicken is simply fabulous! Be prepared for a long line - take it to go as seating area is a bit limited. Delicious roasted Portuguese style chicken. Keep it simple and appreciate the quality of roasted chicken! Parking is tight but you can find spots in the sides streets
The best Portuguese chicken on the planet Plateau -- hands down. Generous portions. Worth lineup when there is one.

Holy moly, $15 large poutine you get a MASSIVE mound of juicy Portuguese chicken, just the right amount of REAL gravy over perfect poutine fries and melty cheese curds. Pleasantly surprised with this find! I also noticed the chicken in the poutine was done/seasoned 2-ways, there was thin slices of (dry rub?) seasoned chicken & then there were pulled apart pieces from a whole Portuguese roasted chicken. We also tried their almond pasteis de Natas which had a more eggy clumpy texture. It was ok.
Long wait, sweet result! There is no many table, so just recomand to go better, English menu is on the wall, inside :)

Our one and only Canadian poutine experience was a bit of a let down. We came last night, and luckily there was no line, so we ordered--ahem, *tried* to order--the poutine with chicken and chorizo and a small green salad. One of us speaks French, and was literally enunciating in a crystal clear manner, "POUTINE AVEC POULET ET CHORIZO" but they were completely befuddled and then tried to claim that they didn't make a small salad, which was right there on their menu, which one of us pointed out. So, not the most welcome introduction or experience. You work your way down the line and pay; the woman at the register was literally standing there eating a yogurt while we were waiting, so don't set those customer service standards too high--it doesn't get better. When we went to go sit down, every single spot was completely filthy and we had to wipe down the tables ourselves. Getting to the actual food: the salad was an afterthought, with a heap of dressing tossed on top in a pool, so, non merci. The "celebrated" poutine was only OK. The chorizo tasted cold and bland and more like a hot dog. We liked the gravy, but it seemed like there was a trace of something sweet in it which we did not appreciate. The chicken was good, but there were massively large and unappetizing pieces of chicken fat thrown in there, and everything was just drowning in the curds and sauce, etc. It was too much, and not in a good way. We were debating whether to go to the other famous place across the street and really wish that we had! Do NOT recommend. 2.5 stars, rounding down.
So good. Best Portuguese chicken. Clean and nice interior. Service somewhat slow but worth the wait.

Hands down the best poutine I've ever had. The enhancements they add here (chicken, sausage) strictly enhance an already great dish. The smokiness and savoriness of these added elements add further depth, and extra protein to boot. The portion size for the large is quite generous, so definitely shareable. This place is bustling, but the staff is efficient with taking orders so don't be intimated if there's a line. Finding a spot to sit is tricky- if coming with other people I recommend dividing and conquering by having someone snag seats while the others order food. A must-try if you're in Montreal!
Chicken breast Poutine Salad Sauce Rice Dessert Everything is good and healthy and delicious
Great portion for affordable price! 10/10 The place is kinda small but the food is delicious. Would def come back when I come visit Montreal

The line to this place was out the door and there's a reason for that. My fiancé got of course a chicken sandwich which he absolutely raved about. They are known for their chicken and poutine so getting one of the two or both is a must. For myself I got the calamari and the veggie salad which also delivered. The nonstop line and crowds of people tells you everything you need to know!

This was a very satisfying lunch. We ordered the Chicken sandwiches, Half chicken, Poutine, and Portuguese tart. The roasted chicken had a deliciously fragrant and flavorful skin, and the meat was juicy and full of flavor. The kitchen's on-site roasting technique really added to the flavor of the chicken. The chicken sandwiches were also very juicy and flavorful. The Portuguese tart was more solid compared to the soft, warm, custardy ones found in Asia, but both are unique and worth trying. The poutine was a classic sausages version and met the expected standard. The portion sizes were very generous, and we couldn't finish it all. So, if you have to choose, definitely start with their chicken, which is really flavorful and juicy despite being dry. Overall, it was a great lunch, and we highly recommend trying the chicken and Portuguese tart.

No stop in Montreal is complete without a taste of poutine. Stopped by here on my last night and so happy I did. Not many people know about this place cause they are so fast to scurry over to the poutine place across the street due to popularity grown through Tiktok. Ma Poule Mouillée serviced superfast with friendly customer experience. I ordered their big plate of poutine to share between me and one other person. Definitely worth to check out!

Best rotisserie chicken I've ever had hands down. Fall off the bone. Insanely flavorful spicy sauce oozing through it. Like it had been marinated for decades in this sauce. Oh and these fries holly cow. Crispy but flavorful. Dipped in the sauce with a bite of the chicken. We went to Michelin level places on our trip in Montreal and this was the best bite. They do poutine too, but I have to recommend the half chicken and fries you don't need any other flavors than that.

Got the small #8 which would have been plenty for two moderately hungry people. Everything was absolutely delicious, the fries held up and remained crispy despite all the toppings, flavors were incredible. Though there was a line it went fairly quickly and was quite efficient!  Excellent place.

This is a must-visit for peri peri chicken in Montreal and the Portuguese egg custard tarts which were a surprise and delight. Be sure to know what you want as you get in line to keep things moving along - the line can be long but it moves decently quickly. My go to is the half chicken with fries and salad and the poutine which comes with a nice savory gravy. Portions are very very generous so an entree can likely last 2 meals. Be sure to grab a few egg tarts after - just trust me on that.

I did not know that I love Portuguese roast chicken -- until I tried it.  Not in Portugal, but in Montreal. Ma Poule Moullée makes one thing -- roast chicken -- and the've perfected the process.  Great food.  The pier pier sauce is lovely and spicy -- so spicy that it's un-Canadian.  Inexpensive. Super fast service. Huge portions. The eating space inside is pretty "rough and ready" as Paul Hollywood says. It looks like most people are picking up to take the food with them. Did I mention the portions are huge? The leg quarter comes with a huge salad. huge amount of fries, a thigh and two drumsticks.  Unless you're a teenager, it's enough for two.

Whoever associated Canadians and maple syrup was wack because Canadians don't really eat that ever. Poutine? Definitely. La Banquise is just across the street and we can have a war about which is better but you can't go wrong with either :) Torn because I love them both --- Ma Poule Mouillée is definitely known for their chicken. Combine that on the poutine with chorizo, gravy and cheese curds, and you've got a hella good combo here! I liked La Banquise cheese curds and gravy a lot better though. Like I said, can't go wrong :) Portuguese egg tarts were amazing though, couldn't stop myself for getting just one!

When in Montreal Poutine is a must! One that truly stood out in my research for great poutine was Ma Poule Mouilee!! The restaurant is popular with constant lineup, but they are very quick. I got in within 15 mins wait. What is unique about this place is they don't make any poutine but one that is topped with freshly grilled Portuguese chicken shreds and chorizo too! It was absolutely poutine heaven!  The grilled chicken was so tender and juicy and there was so much gravy and cheese curd every single bite of fries had just enough of it! Portion was HUGE! With the regular size for $18 the two of us barely managed to finish it! They do have a petite option too that is not so petite at all and would be great for sharing too for those who like to eat lighter.  Not only do they have poutine and chicken but several Portuguese desserts too! I was very tempted but had to hold back because I was just too full. This will definitely be a place I would revisit when I come to Montreal again.

The line was very long even at 5:30pm on a weekday, which surprised me. Cannot imagine coming here on a weekend night during prime dinner hours. The poutine was great, if just slightly too salty. The chicken was great but it's covered in way too many fries. The chicken was barely visible under the pile of fries as you can see in the attached image, but it was some of the best rotisserie-style chicken I've had. I ate the extra fries with the poutines as a starch to help season the fries and offset some of the extra sauce/saltiness in the poutine. I do want to mention that the poutine wasn't overly salty, but I can definitely taste the salt.

Best poutine ever in the whole city ! The chicken is excellent, probably the best as well. They should buy the building next door to expansion the place because it's always super crowded (that's because it's so good). I highly recommend it

Food was great. Can definitely understand why this is a Montreal fave. The line can be a good wait but it's definitely worth it. Menu is on the wall and once you order they are pretty to get your food and pay. This is very casual dining with limited seating inside. Overall a good lunch choice. #8 Poutine Large is a good size for 3 people.
My first poutine ever! It was so yummy. I loved that it wasn't too hot and everything was balanced (not too much gravy) Quick to order. So much food.

If I could have any single meal in Montréal again, it would be this chicken. The sauce was spectacular and you can taste the char from the coals the chicken is roasted over. The fries are perfect sopping up the sauce and the tang and acidity of the salad cut the fat perfectly. Sure the line is long, but it moves quickly. Absolutely perfect.
Sadly, the poutine was cold and limp.  Asked for spicy and got regular. Advice: stick to the chicken, fries, and salad.  My wife had it and is was stellar.
Fabulous food! The place is tiny so it's more a take out place than a sit down restaurant. Get the egg tarts since they are AMAZING and super affordable!

This place is tuned like a fine oiled machine. U get in and order within mins and get your food quick. We got the #2 and #8 and ended up being too much food for the 4 of us. Would recommend the food for sure. Service was excellent and quick.

I arrived in Montreal for the first time in 5 years and this is the first place I went. Brilliant choice because it started my trip off VERY right. La Banquise is across the street from this establishment and many will say that's the best poutine in Montreal but they would be wrong. VERY wrong. The best poutine is at Ma Poule Mouillee and for $12, you get a whole lot of it so bring your friends and your appetites! Chicken, sausage, curds, fries, gravy, sauces, delicious! Everything else is great. Their chicken is delicious and for me, superior to one of their main competitors, Romados. It's just so flavourful and juicy and everything you'd want from Portuguese chicken. The salad and potatoes are also solid. I really don't think you could go wrong with anything here, especially when you consider that they are quite inexpensive. They have a knack for flavours and they deliver excellence every time.
